correctness.rationale: For the stated 16-vertex Cayley graph with step set ±(1,0), ±(0,1), ±(1,1), independent exhaustive enumeration gives 48 edges, exactly two shared neighbors for every pair, 176 connected triples, 60 qualifying four-subsets (48 with five graph edges and 12 induced four-cycles), no qualifying five-subset, hence Alexander dual face counts (1,16,120,176,60). Each of the sixty tetrahedra possesses at least two private triangular facets, so the specified sixty elementary collapses leave a 2-dimensional complex Y with complete K16 one-skeleton and 116 triangles. An independently constructed signed 105x116 boundary matrix in a fundamental-cycle basis has Hermite normal form I105, proving integer surjectivity and no torsion, with H2(Y;Z)=Z^11 and H1=0. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality sends dual degree 2 to original degree 16-2-3=11, with unique reduced H11=Z^11. No 5-vertex dual faces entails full 10-skeleton of the original, hence 9-connectivity; H10=0 and Hurewicz give 10-connectivity; maps representing H11 generators plus homological Whitehead yield the wedge of eleven S11. Original has 13-vertex facets, so dimension 12 and its H11 obstruction proves nonshellability. Every conclusion is for this fixed graph only, and the finite certificate does not assert any all-graph statement.
residual_risks: Integer Hermite normal form is a finite exact algorithm, independently implemented here; it is not a formal proof checker.
Non-equivariant homotopy only; the full automorphism representation was not computed.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge original fixed-graph ordinary three-cut homotopy classification. Independent searches identified the foundational ordinary cut-complex definition but no Shrikhande value, and the nearest same-cut-size rook result has rank 27 only for the nonisomorphic K4 square K4. Theorem 6.1 of Bayer et al. cannot give the present result: its complete (n-k-2)=11 skeleton hypothesis fails, since the sixty connected four-subsets omit sixty 12-vertex faces from the cut complex. The 2024 sequel concerns disjoint unions, squared paths and rectangular path-grid graphs. The four-cycle-free and high-girth theorems do not apply to the 32-triangle/12-induced-four-cycle Shrikhande graph. Related Shrikhande independence and Čech complexes are different functors with different simplices; their homology does not imply this result. The claim has no asserted generalization beyond the fixed graph. Web and indexed-record negative hits do not establish global novelty; priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible older calculation of the Shrikhande connected-triple Alexander dual may exist.

checked_sources: Assigned RESULT.md and independently verified full boundary computation
value.rationale: The two 16-vertex strongly regular graphs with parameters (16,6,2,2), Shrikhande and 4x4 rook, are a canonical pair with the same local numerical parameters. A complete integral homotopy type for the ordinary three-cut complex of the Shrikhande member is a naturally motivated missing exact invariant, not an arbitrary slice. Its rank 11 is distinct from the previously established rank 27 for the other member, showing that this cut-topology invariant is not determined by the usual strongly regular parameters. The result determines torsion-freeness, all homology degrees, a genuine wedge homotopy equivalence, and a non-shellability obstruction in a pure 12-complex, all supported by a nontrivial integral certificate. It does not claim to be the first invariant distinguishing the pair, nor a general classification.
residual_risks: Single fixed graph and ordinary cut size k=3; no statement for all strongly regular graphs.
No equivariant homology or general formula for higher cut sizes.

limitations: The theorem is a finite, exact mathematical classification for one labeled graph; no all-graphs claim.
The finite integer computation is independently reproduced but not formalized in Lean or externally attested.
Priority is best-of-knowledge, with residual risk of unindexed work and no unsupported novelty guarantee.
